profile.reading:
This building, VA16, sits on Vantage's Ashburn I campus at 45200 Vantage Data Plaza, Sterling, VA 20166, per this registry's address matching; Vantage does not publish an individual facility page or press release for VA16 specifically. Vantage's current campus page describes Ashburn I as 52 acres with six data centers totaling 1.7 million square feet at full buildout and 206 megawatts of critical IT load, a building count matching the VA11 through VA16 numbering tracked in this registry (VA11 at 30MW, VA12 at 32MW, and VA13 at 44MW are individually confirmed via Vantage press releases elsewhere in this registry), though Vantage does not explicitly confirm on its own site that VA16 specifically is one of the six, and no individual sqft or MW figure for VA16 is published anywhere found this session.

Vantage is a private, Denver, Colorado-headquartered operator; DigitalBridge acquired the company in March 2017, and in January 2024 Vantage announced a $6.4 billion equity investment round led by DigitalBridge and Silver Lake. Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to every Ashburn-area facility: in November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates raising a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 data center rate class effective January 1, 2027, per Inside Climate News.

Northern Virginia's Loudoun and Prince William counties together form the largest data center market in the world by capacity, and local zoning debate has intensified as residents, county supervisors, and Dominion Energy weigh the tradeoff between commercial tax revenue and rising transmission-line construction, land consumption, and residential electricity-rate pressure tied to data center growth. Dominion Energy's long-range integrated resource plans have repeatedly cited this region's data center demand as the single largest driver of the utility's near-term generation and transmission capital spending, a dynamic that has drawn scrutiny from the Virginia State Corporation Commission in periodic rate cases. As documented in this profile's address and campus fields, this building's assignment to the Vantage campus it is grouped under is inferred from building-count and geographic proximity matching against Vantage's own published campus materials rather than from a Vantage-confirmed individual building name, so it should be read as a reasonable but unconfirmed placement pending direct operator confirmation.

reading.body:
Vantage VA16 is one building in the Ashburn I campus, a six-building complex in Sterling, Virginia that the operator publishes as 206 MW of critical IT load across 1.7 million square feet at full buildout. The operator describes densities up to 300 W per square foot, which implies the campus could eventually host roughly 5,400 racks at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, though no individual building figure is published for VA16 itself.

The Ashburn I campus sits just outside the rank of the 23 published-capacity data centers in Virginia, which collectively claim 1,375 MW. This means the campus, at its stated full capacity, would represent 15% of Virginia's published AI-relevant power capacity and rank it first by a significant margin, though the operator has not published individual building figures that would show how much is already operational versus planned.

Virginia hosts 326 mapped data center facilities, but only 23 publish power specifications to operators' spec pages. The state context given does not indicate grid interconnection status, power source, or timeline to capacity for Ashburn I or this building, so whether this campus can realistically reach its stated 206 MW under Virginia's current and projected power availability cannot be determined from the published facts.
